extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary examiners) and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on when and how to make rejections (especially final rejections) in patent prosecution, including required statements of grounds, form-paragraph use, handling previously allowed claims, IDS effects, and special rules for first-action finals and RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact prosecution – initial comprehensive review
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the principles of compact prosecution, each claim should be reviewed for compliance with every statutory requirement for patentability in the initial review of the application, even if one or more claims are found to be deficient with respect to some statutory requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies should be explained clearly, particularly when they serve as a basis for a rejection. Whenever practicable, USPTO personnel should indicate how rejections may be overcome and how problems may be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full development of non-prior-art rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a rejection not based on prior art is proper (lack of adequate written description, enablement, or utility, etc.) such rejection should be stated with a full development of the reasons rather than by a mere conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description, enablement), lack of utility, nonstatutory subject matter — explain thoroughly and indicate how to overcome if practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great care when rejecting previously allowed claims; primary examiner signature
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable may be rejected only after a primary examiner has considered all the facts. An Office action rejecting a previously allowed claim must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care should be exercised. When a previously-allowed claim is withdrawn, use Form Paragraph 7.50. The Office action should point out that the claim was previously allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review previous examiner work; avoid wholesale reorientation
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigned to act on an application which has received one or more actions by some other examiner, the examiner should review the previous search to ensure it is thorough and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, an examiner should not take an entirely new approach or attempt to reorient the point of view of a previous examiner, or make a new search in the mere hope of finding something (see MPEP § 904.02 and cited case law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat and clearly state all grounds in a final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In making such final rejection, the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable to the claims in the application, clearly stating the reasons in support thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before final rejection a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and applicant. All outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed and reiterated in the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds development for appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rejection must be clearly developed to such an extent that applicant may readily judge the advisability of an appeal unless a single previous Office action contains a complete statement supporting the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement, the final rejection may refer to it but should include a rebuttal of any arguments raised in applicant’s reply. Examiner’s answer should contain a complete statement of the examiner’s position if appeal is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form Paragraph 7.39 to conclude final rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rejection letter should conclude with Form Paragraph 7.39 (Action Is Final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form Paragraph 7.39 contains information on shortened statutory period (three months), extension policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a), and examiner notes about exceptions (reissue litigation, reexamination). Use 7.39.01 for pro se applicant notifications and ensure required preceding paragraphs when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a clear issue before making a rejection final
rubrics_metrics.description: Before final rejection is in order a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reach early termination (allowance or final rejection) the invention should be thoroughly searched in the first action and the references fully applied; avoid switching subject matter in successive amendments or successive examiner reference sets because that defeats clearly defined issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-or-subsequent-action finality rule
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final, whereupon applicant's reply is limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a second or subsequent action shall not be made final if the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment nor based on an information disclosure statement (IDS) filed during the set period with fee. See 37 CFR 1.113 and MPEP § 609.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-with-fee triggered finality and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in an information disclosure statement during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final whether or not the claims have been amended, provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.40.01 should be used when an IDS-with-fee prompted the new ground(s) making the action final. Examiner must not make final where there is another new ground not necessitated by amendment nor based on such IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newly-cited art and first/second-action finality limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or any subsequent action will not be made final if it includes a rejection on newly cited art other than IDS-with-fee of any claim not amended or amended in a way that does not necessitate a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims are treated as amended if the independent claim or any claim it references is amended. See MPEP § 821.04 et seq. and guidance on what constitutes a new ground in MPEP § 1207.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make final when prior art is not of record for amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent action should not be made final if it includes a rejection on prior art not of record of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner cannot be expected to foresee every applicant amendment, but should avoid finalizing when prior art not previously of record is applied to claims that could reasonably have been expected as filed. See MPEP § 904 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate common-ownership or JRA statements when applying certain references
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying any 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) or pre-AIA 102(e)/103 references, the examiner should anticipate that a statement averring common ownership may qualify applicant for exceptions under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) or that a statement of common ownership at the time the invention was made may disqualify a patent or application applied in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a statement is filed in reply and the claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made. See MPEP §§ 2146.03 and 2154.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Research Agreement (JRA) exception/disqualification may necessitate new double patenting rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reference’s subject matter is excepted as prior art under the JRA provision or disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c) and a pending rejection is thereby overcome, the examiner may need to make a new double patenting rejection based upon the excepted/disqualified reference; the next Office action may be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new double patenting rejection is proper because it was necessitated by applicant amendment or IDS; the examiner may make that next action final provided no other new grounds are introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating art as current vs pre-AIA 102 may allow final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the only changes in a rejection are based on treating the application as subject to current 35 U.S.C. 102 rather than pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (or vice versa), and any prior art relied upon was prior art under both versions, then the action may be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: first action relied upon a reference under pre-AIA 102(e) and subsequent action relies on same reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2); the subsequent action may be final assuming no new non-prior-art rejections were made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allow claims amended without showing patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant amends the claims without attempting to show patentable novelty, the examiner should not allow the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may be finally rejected if, in the opinion of the examiner, they are clearly open to rejection on grounds of record. See MPEP § 714.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.40 family for finals necessitated by amendment (and variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.40 should be used where an action is made final including new grounds of rejection necessitated by applicant’s amendment. Variants (7.40.01, 7.40.02.aia, 7.40.02.fti) cover IDS-with-fee, invoking JRA under AIA, and pre-AIA JRA disqualification respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each variant has examiner notes about when it must/should not be used and what information (e.g., dates) to insert in brackets. Follow the limitations in the form-paragraph notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection on first action (continuing/substitute applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new application, claims may be finally rejected in the first Office action when (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims of the new application (1) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with, the claims in the earlier application, and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits first-action finals in continuing/substitute scenarios where the claims are essentially the same as previously examined claims and the rejection basis is unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection following RCE (conditions analogous to first-action final)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application in which an RCE has been filed, claims may be finally rejected in the first action following the filing of the RCE when all claims after entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the claims before the RCE and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note applicants cannot use an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from, or lack unity of invention with, previously examined claims (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions). See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 706.07(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirements and consequences of final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to a final rejection must include cancellation of, or appeal from the rejection of, each rejected claim. Filing an amendment after final rejection does not stop the running of the statutory period for reply unless the examiner holds all claims to be in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires to appeal, a Notice of Appeal must be filed within the period for reply with the fee (37 CFR 41.20(b)(1)). After final, applicant may file RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 where permitted; failure to timely respond will result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 should be used in all Office actions up to and including final rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form to summarize the action; for amendments filed after final rejection see MPEP §§ 714.12 and 714.13.
